card.title: Nucleus — binding energy, nuclear fission and fusion

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: A nucleus is lighter than its free nucleons by the mass defect, and that mass is the binding energy, with 1 u equal to 931 MeV. Stability follows the binding energy per nucleon, which peaks near iron. Fission of heavy nuclei and fusion of light nuclei both move toward that peak and release energy.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: The mass of a nucleus is less than the mass of its separated protons and neutrons. The difference is the mass defect. It is not a mistake in the weighing. It is the mass equivalent of the binding energy.  ·  Binding energy = Δm c^2. In nuclear units, 1 u corresponds to 931 MeV. The binding energy is the energy you would have to supply to pull the nucleus apart into free nucleons.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: Mass defect  ·  Binding energy per nucleon  ·  Fission  ·  Fusion

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: The nucleus is lighter than its free nucleons.  ·  The missing mass is the binding energy.  ·  Per nucleon, the curve peaks near iron.  ·  Fission and fusion both move toward that peak.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Mass defect Δm = Z m_p + N m_n − M; binding energy BE = Δm c²; BE per nucleon peaks near Fe-56 (~8.8 MeV).  ·  Radioactive decay: N = N₀e^(−λt), t_½ = ln2/λ; activity A = λN.

rows.label: More practice
rows.text: Why do both fission and fusion release energy?

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: The useful comparison between nuclei is the binding energy per nucleon, the total divided by the mass number A. It is low for the very light nuclei, highest near iron, and a little lower again for the heavy nuclei.  ·  Fission splits a very heavy nucleus into two medium ones. Those pieces sit higher on the curve, so energy is released. A chain reaction needs neutrons from one fission to cause the next.  ·  Fusion joins very light nuclei into a heavier one that is higher on the curve. That also releases energy. It is the energy source of the Sun. The nuclei must be brought close enough for the strong force to act, which means a very high temperature.

rows.text: ❌ skip the key fact → ✅ mass defect δm = z m_p + n m_n − m; binding energy be = δm c²; be per nucleon peaks near fe-56 (~8.8 mev)..  ·  A larger mass defect means more tightly bound, not heavier.  ·  Per nucleon is the stability comparison.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Fusion is for light nuclei and fission is for heavy nuclei.  ·  1 u is 931 MeV, not 931 J.  ·  Say per nucleon when you mean the curve.
